Writing a Custom Agent ​

This guide builds a research specialist, puts it in a department, and gives its lead the ability to route work to it.

1. Create the agent ​

Ask PRIME, or call the tool:

create_agent(
  name: "research",
  description: "Market and competitor research; produces sourced briefs.",
  department: "Growth",
  permission: "custom",
  tools: ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "WebFetch", "WebSearch"]
)

That scaffolds agents/research/ with an AGENT.md.

2. Write AGENT.md ​

markdown
---
description: Market and competitor research; produces sourced briefs.
department: Growth
lead: false
permission: custom
tools: [Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch, WebSearch]
model: claude-opus-5
effort: medium
---

You are Saidi's research specialist.

## What you do
Answer market, competitor, and pricing questions with sourced briefs. Every claim
carries its source URL inline.

## How you work
- Prefer primary sources: filings, changelogs, pricing pages, official docs.
- When two sources disagree, say so and give both.
- Never state a number without a date attached to it.

## What you never do
- Never present a vendor's marketing copy as a finding.
- Never guess at a figure you could not find. Say it is not public.

The body is the persona prompt. The frontmatter is configuration:

KeyEffect
descriptionShown in list_agents, and how PRIME decides to route to it
departmentGroups it with its team
leadtrue gives it delegation tools over its department
permissionall | read-only | custom
toolsExact allow-list when permission: custom
model / profile / effortDefaults; empty means inherit

Write the description for the router, not for a human

PRIME picks an agent from its description. "Market and competitor research; produces sourced briefs" routes correctly. "Helps with research stuff" does not.

3. Add skills ​

Skills are reusable procedures the agent can invoke.

add_skill(agent: "research", name: "competitor-teardown", content: "...")
import_skill(agent: "research", url: "https://example.com/skills/pricing-scan.md")

They land in agents/research/skills/.

4. Give it MCP servers ​

add_mcp_server(agent: "research", name: "notion", config: { ... })

This writes agents/research/.mcp.json. Only that agent gets those servers — this is the main reason to split a capability into its own agent rather than widening PRIME's belt.

5. Make a lead ​

Set lead: true on one agent in the department:

markdown
---
description: Growth department lead. Routes research, content, and analysis work.
department: Growth
lead: true
permission: all
---

The lead is spawned with a different toolbelt:

  • delegate_to_specialist and delegate_to_specialists — scoped to the other agents in Growth, plus a prompt fragment naming the team.
  • Its own delegate_to_project, scoped to the department's projects, if any are mapped.

A lead with no team members and no projects gets no delegation tools — there is nothing to route to.

6. Give it memory ​

remember(scope: "agent", name: "research", facts: [
  "Pricing pages for the three tracked competitors are archived monthly in the Growth Notion DB.",
  "Never cite Crunchbase headcount figures — they lag by two quarters."
])

Agent memory lives in memory/agents/research.md and is injected into every spawn.

7. Test it ​

Run it read-only first:

run_agent(agent: "research", task: "Summarise how the three tracked competitors price their team tier. Cite each source.")

Check the report against the contract: verdict first, one line per thing asked, proof inline. If the agent returns a wall of narration, the persona needs tightening, not the task.
